newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian protests over election "fraud" roll on.
newsitem.headline: Serbian protests over election "fraud" roll on.

text.p: Serbian opposition leaders said on Tuesday their protests were gaining momentum and vowed to keep up pressure on President Slobodan Milosevic to recognise the results of local elections that went againt him.
Several thousand students from Belgrade university, who launched a strike on Monday, marched through the capital at midday, chanting against Milosevic's nine-year rule.
"There are no lessons in Belgrade today," one professor told the students. "This is a lesson -- a lesson in democracy."
Joined by several of their professors, the students halted traffic as they marched past foreign embassies in pouring rain.
They hurled eggs and a few stones at offices of the Yugoslav United Left, the party led by Milosevic's Marxist wife. A couple of windows were broken in the otherwise peaceful march.
The students planned sit-ins at five faculties while the opposition scheduled another protest for 1400 GMT.

The Zajedno (Together) coalition has led Serbia's biggest street demonstrations in five years after accusing authorities of stealing their victory in run-off local elections on November 17, by annulling results on the pretext of irregularities.
An opposition demonstration in Belgrade drew an estimated 150,000 on Monday, virtually shutting down the city centre.
Focusing anger on Milosevic's propaganda tools, protesters pelted state newspaper and television offices with eggs.
Zoran Djindjic, a Zajedno leader, told the crowd the former communist party leader's power was under unprecedented threat.
"This is no longer an election rally or a protest rally. This is a democratic revolution that Serbia has been waiting 50 years for," he said.
The United States on Monday condemned the annulment of the municipal election results, which had shown victories for the Zajedno coalition in 15 of the country's 18 biggest towns.

Charges that authorities committed massive fraud prompted the European Union on Monday to postpone giving the Yugoslav republics of Serbia and Montenegro preferential trade status granted to other countries in the region.
Djindjic told Reuters the opposition protests would soon turn into a campaign of civil disobedience.

"Milosevic is a coward. He dares not appear, pretends not to know," he said. "In the end, we will call the people to resort to other methods, to strikes in factories and schools. I think everything is going according to plan."
Despite forecasts of civil disobedience, it remained unclear if the opposition could persuade workers to strike.

Workers from a household appliance factory in the southern town of Nis planned to join demonstrations in that town on Tuesday but there had been no call for a strike, a trade union spokesman said by telephone.

Electoral commissions and courts last week annulled poll results in almost all towns where Zajedno claimed victory. In Belgrade, a municipal court on Sunday stripped Zajedno of a majority in the city council which authorities earlier confirmed.
Electoral commissions have called for another round of voting on Wednesday and Sunday.

Zajedno has urged a boycott of the third round in the capital, calling the vote a "farce". Local opposition leaders in some other towns said they would run in the third round despite their objections.
State media declared that a campaign blackout began at midnight on Sunday, in a tactic analysts say was designed to provide an exuse for ignoring the protests ahead of the polls.
Strong international support was considered crucial for the opposition but Zajedno officials said privately they had received no promises from the West.

The United States and European powers once accused Milosevic of igniting war in the former Yugoslavia. They now view him as a pillar of Balkan peace after he signed the Dayton treaty for Bosnia last year.
Zajedno leaders argue that they too are committed to the Dayton accords and that they advocate democratic and free-market reforms in Serbia which would bring stability to the region.
